problem:
Rewrite the following expression as the difference of a perfect square and a constant.

$({x}^{2}-11x+\frac{121}{4})-10=(x\,\,-$
{{field-1}} $)^{2}-$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a)^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-11x+\frac{121}{4} & = \\ {x}^{2}-11x+{(\frac{11}{2})}^{2} & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{11}{2}x+{(\frac{11}{2})}^{2} & = \\ {(x-\frac{11}{2})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-11x+\frac{121}{4})-10 & = \\ {(x-\frac{11}{2})}^{2}-10 & .\end{aligned}
$$
